questions: Do you have a tremor (shaking) in your hands?
Have you noticed slowness in your movements or in getting dressed/eating?
Do you have pain in your neck?
Have you had difficulty with balance or recent falls?
Has your speech become softer, slurred, or monotone?
Do you feel stiffness or rigidity in your body or neck?
Have you had a stroke in the past?
Has your handwriting become noticeably smaller?
Do you have difficulty turning in bed at night?
Do you have numbness, tingling, or weakness in your arms or legs?
Have you been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease or a similar condition?
Have you had any prior injury or surgery to your neck?
Do you have memory or thinking problems?
Have you lost weight unintentionally over the past several months?
orders: Observation of the tremor at rest, with arms outstretched, and during finger-to-nose testing to characterise rest, postural, and intention components
Spiral-drawing and handwriting assessment to look for tremor frequency/amplitude and micrographia
Examination for cogwheel rigidity at the wrist and elbow with reinforcement
Assessment of bradykinesia using rapid alternating finger taps and fist opening/closing
Gait, stride length, arm swing, and pull-test assessment
Examination for head, voice, and chin tremor
Supine versus standing examination to assess for orthostatic tremor
Serum electrolytes, glucose, and liver function tests
MRI brain if diagnosis remains uncertain after the above
DaT-SPECT scan if parkinsonism still cannot be excluded clinically

1. Enhanced physiological tremor (idiopathic or medication-related)
2. Functional (psychogenic) tremor
3. Focal dystonic tremor of the hand
